question.text: What are 'swaptions' in the interest rate options market?

answer.text: Options on interest rate swaps — the holder has the right to enter into a specific interest rate swap at a future date. A payer swaption gives the right to pay fixed/receive floating; a receiver swaption gives the right to receive fixed/pay floating
A combination of a swap and a futures contract
An option to swap equity holdings for bond holdings
A type of currency swap where the parties can choose whether to exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series IV page 95 defines a swaption as an option on a swap and states that an interest rate swaption gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to enter into an interest rate swap. A receiver/call swaption gives the right to receive fixed and pay floating, while a payer/put swaption gives the right to pay fixed and receive floating. The Trap: A swaption is not a hybrid of a swap and a futures contract, nor an option to exchange equities for bonds. It is also distinct from a generic currency swap with an embedded choice — the source ties the term specifically to options on interest rate swaps. Note: The payer/receiver definitions and the right-not-obligation language follow Series IV page 95 (with the same terminology reiterated on page 154).
